# create_llm_file_tool

> Create text-based LlmDocument files programmatically with content and automatically attach them to the current conversation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `data` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations (default); grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=create_llm_file_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Create text-based LlmDocument files programmatically with content and automatically attach them to the current conversation.
This tool allows AI agents to generate documents (reports, summaries, documentation) that are immediately shared with users.

PICK THE FORMAT FROM THE ASK (text content only — all require the 'content' field):
- "text/markdown" — anything the reader will READ: reports, briefs, notes, specs,
  summaries, meeting minutes, documentation. The default for prose.
- "text/html" — anything the reader will LOOK AT: dashboards, scorecards, trackers,
  status boards, KPI summaries, comparison pages, one-page visual overviews. Send one
  self-contained page (inline <style>, no external assets, no <script> — the preview
  sandbox does not run scripts; draw charts as inline SVG). Markdown tables are not a
  dashboard — if the ask says "dashboard", "scorecard", "board" or "visual", use HTML.
  A "dashboard" skill, when granted, carries the on-brand page template.
- "text/plain", "text/csv" — raw text / tabular data exports
- "application/x-yaml" — config / orchestration pipeline definitions
- Not the right tool for decks, diagrams, infographics, images or PDFs — if a skill or
  tool exists for that output (e.g. office documents, diagram, infographics, image
  generation, pdf_from_markdown), use it rather than describing the visual in text.
- NOT application/pdf or DOCX — string content cannot produce a real binary document;
  upload actual PDF/DOCX bytes via the file upload API (or use convert_to_pdf_tool)

IMAGES (image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, image/svg+xml): EITHER pass
`source_url` (an https URL the server fetches — preferred for anything over a few
hundred KB, because base64 in your context is expensive and can abort the turn) OR the
raw bytes base64-encoded in `content_base64` (no data: URI prefix). Leave `content`
empty. Raster images are validated and normalised on ingest (8-bit PNG/JPEG/WEBP,
metadata stripped, ≤8000px) so vision models can always read them; an undecodable
payload is rejected with a clear error. Stored as an LlmImage.

TARGET CONVERSATION: by default the file attaches to the conversation you are in.
Pass `conversation_id` to attach it to ANOTHER conversation you have write access to
(e.g. the channel that asked for the deliverable) — it is posted there as a message
from you with the file attached.

RULES:
- ALWAYS set directory_path to organize files (e.g. "/sdlc/rate-limiting/").
- Orchestration stage work MUST go under "/Agent Orchestrations/Orchestration <execution-id>";
  stray variants like "/orch-65/..." are rewritten to that canonical directory.
- ALWAYS include the markdown link from the response when referencing the file in a message.
- Give a descriptive title saying what the document contains.
- For audio/video/PDF/DOCX bytes use the file upload API instead.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes | Descriptive title for the file (required). Should clearly explain what the document contains. Example: "Project Analysis Report", "Meeting Summary - Q4 2024", "Generated Documentation". |
| `mime_type` | string | yes | MIME type for text-based documents. Supported types: text/markdown (recommended), text/x-markdown, text/plain, text/csv, text/html, application/json, application/xml, text/xml, application/x-yaml. NOT application/pdf or DOCX — those need real binary bytes via the file upload API. |
| `content` | string | no | Document content (required for text MIME types). For markdown files, provide markdown-formatted text with headers, lists, etc. For text/html, provide a complete self-contained HTML document (inline CSS, inline SVG for charts, no <script>, no external assets). For text files, provide plain text. Not used for image MIME types. |
| `content_base64` | string | no | Base64-encoded file bytes — REQUIRED for image MIME types (image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, image/svg+xml), max 15 MB decoded. No data: URI prefix. |
| `source_url` | string | no | For images: an http(s) URL of the image to fetch server-side instead of base64. Private/internal hosts are blocked. Max 25 MB. |
| `conversation_id` | integer | no | Optional: attach the file to this conversation instead of the current one (you must be a member with write access). Posted as a message from you. |
| `directory_path` | string | no | Virtual directory path for file organization (e.g., "/projects/docs", "/reports/2024"). Defaults to root "/". |

## Example

```json
{"name": "create_llm_file_tool", "arguments": {"title": "Q3 status report", "mime_type": "text/markdown", "content": "# Q3 status\n\n- Revenue up 12%\n- Two hires closed", "directory_path": "/reports/2026"}}
```

Returns the new file's id, title and path. The file is attached to the current conversation
(or to `conversation_id` when given) and is immediately visible to its members.

## Gotchas

- **Pick the MIME type from the ask.** Something to *read* → `text/markdown`; something to
  *look at* (dashboard, scorecard, board) → a single self-contained `text/html` page with
  inline styles and no `<script>`.
- **Images are bytes, not text.** Pass `source_url` (preferred) or `content_base64`; leave
  `content` empty.
- **No PDF or DOCX from a string.** Upload real bytes via the file upload API, or produce a
  PDF from markdown with `convert_to_pdf_tool`.
- **Small edits later:** use [`update_llm_file_tool`](update_llm_file_tool.md) with `replacements`
  instead of resending the whole document.
